current_description.description_long: The Associated Press page cited for this record is headed “Tracking Trump’s presidential promises.” It is a journalism project about promises attributed to Donald Trump, rather than a report documenting the rhetoric or consequences asserted in the earlier description. The source supports a narrow entry about AP publishing a tracker on that subject. The packet does not identify which promise the original writer meant, quote the promise, give a dated progress assessment, or explain the standard used to judge delivery. It also supplies no evidence that Trump’s language shifted, that evaluation criteria were unclear, or that this created particular accountability costs. Those propositions cannot be inferred from the existence of a tracker. This draft therefore confines the claim to the cited project and makes no conclusion about any promise’s status or Trump’s messaging. A specific dated tracker card would be needed to write about an individual commitment or AP’s assessment of it.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Trump Pardons Slew of White-Collar Criminals and Political Allies
proposal.original_synopsis: In a brazen display of corruption, Trump issued a wave of pardons in August 2025 targeting wealthy white-collar criminals and key political allies who had refused to cooperate with investigators. proposal.original_claim_summary: In March 2025 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth restructured military promotions to require political loyalty to Trump over merit and professional qualifications.

identified_problems.explanation: No credible directive or report located establishing an explicit Trump-loyalty requirement in the military promotion system.

Defense Department materials state that promotion and selection decisions should be merit-based, and a June 2025 review memorandum calls for fair, transparent, objective and merit-based promotion procedures. Personnel firings do not establish the claimed promotion loyalty test.

frozen_original.title: Hegseth Restructures Military Promotions to Require Trump Loyalty
frozen_original.synopsis: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth implemented new requirements for military promotions that prioritize political loyalty to Donald Trump over merit, combat experience, and professional qualifications. The restructuring effectively installed a political loyalty test into the armed forces' advancement system, replacing the merit-based system that has governed military promotions since the post-WWII era. Retired generals and military experts warned the changes would devastate military effectiveness, drive away the most capable officers, and compromise national security.

proposal.original_claim_summary: The administration allegedly dismantled First Step Act rehabilitation programs in federal prisons in March 2025.

identified_problems.explanation: No March directive ending all prison education, vocational, treatment and reentry programs was found.
BOP later directed robust implementation of the First Step Act and Second Chance Act, contradicting the claimed wholesale dismantling.

claims.claim: BOP issued a June 2025 directive for robust implementation of the First Step Act and Second Chance Act.
All non-security rehabilitation programming was ended in March 2025.

frozen_original.title: Trump Ends Federal Prisoner Rehabilitation Programs
frozen_original.synopsis: In March 2025, the Trump administration dismantled the First Step Act implementation infrastructure — the bipartisan prison reform law passed in 2018 — by eliminating federal funding for prison education programs, vocational training, substance abuse treatment, and re-entry support services for incarcerated people. The Bureau of Prisons was directed to cease all programming not directly related to security and to abolish positions for educators, counselors, and social workers at federal facilities. Recidivism research had consistently shown that education and vocational programs dramatically reduced re-offense rates and saved far more than their cost. The administration simultaneously pursued longer mandatory minimum sentences for drug and immigration offenses. Criminal justice reformers from across the political spectrum, including many conservatives who had championed the First Step Act, condemned the dismantling as both cruel and counterproductive.
